verdict.rationale: Neon's hosted MCP server exposes SQL tools (Run SQL, Run SQL Transaction, Explain) and schema-migration tools (Prepare/Complete Database Migration, Compare schema). It also documents least-privilege controls: a `?readonly=true` mode, `?category=` tool scoping, and project scoping. A keyless probe confirmed that a readonly/querying config returns only tools flagged `readOnlySafe: true` and injects a notice that all write-access tools have been removed. missing for 10: independent community corroboration of agents using these scoped modes in practice, and explicit evidence of per-tool destructive annotations beyond the readOnlySafe flag.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can run SQL and schema operations through scoped tools that distinguish read-only from destructive actions, so I can safely delegate database work

citations.quote: schema work ("Prepare Database Migration", "Complete Database Migration", "Compare database schema")
a read-only mode via `?readonly=true` ("Limit tools to read-safe actions. Good default for exploration"), tool-category scoping via repeatable `?category=<name>` parameters
every tool carries "readOnlySafe": true and JSON-Schema inputs
All write-access tools have been removed. All remaining tools are limited to read-only operations
The `inspect_database` tool "runs inside a read-only transaction"
